Store the clusterings of the default heatmaps

Source: R/utils_markers.R
update_default_clusterings.Rd

Cluster the metacells of the heatmap that each heatmap tab (Markers, Gene modules, Inner-fold, Stdev-fold, Projected-fold and Outliers) starts with, and store the clusterings in the project, so that the app doesn't cluster them the first time a tab is opened, which takes minutes for large datasets. import_dataset already does this. Use this function for projects imported with an older version of MCView, or after changing the gene modules with update_gene_modules.

Usage

update_default_clusterings(project, overwrite = FALSE)

Arguments

project

path to the project directory

overwrite

recompute the clusterings of datasets that already have them

Details

Under the hood - MCView writes a file named "default_clusterings.qs2" under project/cache/dataset, and skips datasets whose directory is a symlink to outside the project. When that directory isn't writable and the environment variable MCVIEW_CLUSTERING_CACHE_DIR is set, the clusterings are stored in that directory instead. Apps that set the variable (e.g. all the apps of a shiny server) also store there every clustering they compute and look for clusterings there, so each clustering is computed once per server rather than once per app process. (MCVIEW_SHINY_CACHE_DIR keeps the apps' plots and tables across restarts in the same way, see run_app.)

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
update_default_clusterings("PBMC")
} # }
